facts.raw_span: A patient in their 80s with a history of hypertension
1 episode of syncope
feeling hot and light-headed
a few near-fainting spells in the week prior to this index syncopal event
Vital signs were stable without considerable orthostatic changes in blood pressure and heart rate
Serum electrolyte levels and cardiac enzymes were normal
Cranial CT: No acute pathologic changes
Echocardiogram: Mild concentric left ventricular hypertrophy with preserved left ventricular systolic function
Sinus rhythm with right bundle-branch block
Left anterior fascicular block
PR interval of 204 milliseconds
Premature atrial complex at rate of 64 beats per minute

rationales.F01: Hypertension is a risk factor for hypertensive heart disease
rationales.F02: Syncope can be a symptom of various cardiac and non-cardiac conditions
rationales.F04: Near-fainting spells may indicate a condition that affects blood pressure regulation
rationales.F05: Stable vital signs without orthostatic changes make orthostatic hypotension less likely
rationales.F06: Normal serum electrolyte levels and cardiac enzymes reduce the likelihood of certain cardiac conditions
rationales.F07: No acute pathologic changes on cranial CT rule out intracranial hemorrhage
rationales.F08: Mild concentric left ventricular hypertrophy is consistent with hypertensive heart disease
rationales.F09: Sinus rhythm with right bundle-branch block may indicate a cardiac conduction disease
rationales.F10: Left anterior fascicular block is a type of cardiac conduction disease
rationales.F11: Prolonged PR interval may indicate a cardiac conduction disease

frontier_selector.why: The presence of sinus rhythm with right bundle-branch block, left anterior fascicular block, and PR interval of 204 milliseconds specifically supports Cardiac Conduction Disease.
